item.title: [ZEPPELIN-1560] NPE in SparkInterpreter.java of Zeppelin 0.6.2 interpreter when running Zeppelin 0.6.2 with Spark 2.0.1 or Spark 1.6.1

Hi, moon! Sorry for the late reply due to transferring to other issues.
For this NPE issue, it will occur when you use IBM jre 8 to run spark 161 or spark 201. I have checked, when you use IBM java to run spark master, then no matter which java we are using to run Zeppelin, we will encounter this issue occasionally. I checked the code logic in SparkInterpreter.java of Zeppelin, take the case of Spark 2.x as an example: 

binder = (Map<String, Object>) getLastObject();

the above getLastObject() returned null, and traced back, it's the following method (Utils.invokeMethod(intp, "lastRequest")) that was called returned null.

  public Object getLastObject() {
    IMain.Request r = (IMain.Request) Utils.invokeMethod(intp, "lastRequest");
    if (r == null || r.lineRep() == null) {
      return null;
    }
    Object obj = r.lineRep().call("$result",
        JavaConversions.asScalaBuffer(new LinkedList<Object>()));
    logger.info("obj call object is:" + obj);
    return obj;
  }

And this Utils.invokeMethod(intp, "lastRequest") is a method API that included in scala.tools.nsc.interpreter.IMain tool of scala Interpreter. I added some more interpreter("cmd") command lines to give to scala interpreter, like adding 

      interpret("val a = 1");
      int returnValue = (int) getLastObject();

before and after this command line :

interpret("@transient val _binder = new java.util.HashMap[String, Object]()");

just found the scala interpreter went down before it wants to create this _binder object when this error issue occurred.
So it could be something with Spark, that's why when spark is running on a different Java, then this issue occurred. Do you have any idea about why this came out or how to work around this?
Thanks again.
\cc Luciano Resende

Investigating this with Sherry, current theory is that there's a race condition whereby lastRequest can be null more often with IBM's JDK. As _binder is immutable we can't have something else setting this to be null and we know it's not to do with the HashMap implementation (that does differ between vendors) owing to Sherry's val a = 1 test failing.

Need to find what we should lock on and I think we're missing a synchronized call somewhere so we'll investigate by programatically getting a javacore of all threads when it passes and when it fails - checking the order of execution for methods in each thread:

public Object getLastObject() {

IMain.Request r = (IMain.Request) Utils.invokeMethod(intp, "lastRequest");  
  if (r == null) {
    System.out.println("R is null, will fail");
   } else {
     System.out.println("R is not null, will pass");
   }
   com.ibm.jvm.Dump.JavaDump();

I think the current logic assumes once we have our input (from the point of pressing shift+enter to interpret) we're good to process said command, but actually this isn't the case as we have to make a few expensive reflection calls upfront.

Note that this NPE is fatal, a restart of the Zeppelin daemon is required, and this will impact all IBM Java users of Zeppelin.

The scala compilation is failing causing this error. In the failing case in scala.tools.nsc.Interpreter.IMain.ReadEvalPrint the generated package name is invalid as the lineId is a negative number and so the package name contains a '-' eg

package $line-4968254721

so it looks like the lineId is getting an uninitialized value??

for that package name to be negative, that package name value is produced by Zeppelin 0.6. 2source code SparkInterpreter.java in line 754:

System.setProperty("scala.repl.name.line", "$line" + this.hashCode());

and for openjdk, hashCode() will always return the positive value, but when running with IBM java, that could be a negative value, that's why this string "package $line-4968254721" popped up, and some test performed with hashCode() running with IBM jdk and openjdk, for 10000 times, with openjdk we got Non-negative value number as 10000, no negative number show up. However, when running with IBM java, got Non-neg: 5106 neg: 4894. Which explains why we sometimes meet with the error, and sometimes we just pass with success.
Wow, it's good research!!
OK so this is a zeppelin issue as it is perfectly valid for hashCode to return a negative integer,

Discussed with Pete, according to Java specification, hashCode() is allowed to return negative Int. OpenJdk always returns positive is just an implementation detail. So suggest to fix it from Zeppelin side, how do you think about it?
\cc Lee moon soo
\cc Jongyoul Lee

And btw, is there any plan for Zeppelin 0.7.0 to release, like the estimated release date? Could you help inform us?

Thanks in advance!

a very simple fix would be to replace the '-' with another character such as '_' to ensure a valid package name is generated eg:

System.setProperty("scala.repl.name.line", ("$line" + this.hashCode()).replace('-', '_'));

jongyoul moon Is this a fix we could get in ASAP?
